+---
+name: committing
+description: Use when creating git commits in Megatron-Energon. Covers Conventional Commit format, scopes, sign-off, and checking commits locally.
+---
+
+<!--- Copyright (c) 2025, NVIDIA CORPORATION.
+SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause -->
+
+# Committing
+
+The authoritative rules are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) and
+[Signing Your Work](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#signing-your-work). Summary:
+
+## Format
+
+```
+<type>(<scope>): <description>
+
+[optional body]
+```
+
+- `type`: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `style`, `chore`,
+  `revert`.
+- `scope` (optional): affected area, e.g. `loader`, `sampler`, `recipe`, `flavors`, `wrappers`,
+  `task_encoder`, `cache`, `av`, `cli`.
+- `description`: imperative mood, lowercase start, no trailing period.
+- Breaking changes: add `!` after the scope (`refactor(recipe)!: ...`) and explain in the body.
+- Pull requests are merged without squashing: every commit must follow the format.
+
+## Rules
+
+- Always sign off: `git commit -s`. The human you work for signs off and is responsible.
+- Never add `Co-Authored-By` (or similar) trailers for AI assistants.
+- One concern per commit. Run `just fix` and `just check` before committing.
+- Before finishing, run `just check-commits` to validate sign-off and format of the branch.
+- Never push unless the human explicitly asks.

+# Opening a pull request
+
+Policy lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md); the template is
+`.github/pull_request_template.md`.
+
+## Agent rules
+
+- Only push, open a PR or issue, or comment on GitHub when the human explicitly asks.
+- Open PRs as **drafts** and fill in every section of the template.
+- Leave the "I, a human, have personally reviewed every line" checkbox **unticked**. Only the human
+  may tick it; CI fails until they do.
+- Never post review replies or comments on the human's behalf unless asked.
+
+## Before opening
+
+1. `just fix`, `just check` and `just test` pass.
+2. `just check-commits` passes (Conventional Commits, `Signed-off-by` of the commit author).
+3. User-facing changes have docs in `docs/source`.
+4. The branch is focused on a single concern.
+

+
+- **What does this PR do?** What and why, briefly.
+- **Linked issue:** required for external contributors (`Fixes #123`). Issues must describe a real
+  problem encountered while using Energon, not automated or speculative findings.
+- **Testing:** exact commands that were run and their results.

+---
+name: writing-tests
+description: Use when adding or changing tests in Megatron-Energon, or when a code change needs test coverage. Covers the end-to-end test style, dataset fixtures, save/restore and multi-worker checks, and how to run focused tests.
+---
+
+<!--- Copyright (c) 2025, NVIDIA CORPORATION.
+SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause -->
+
+# Writing tests
+
+Tests use `unittest`, not `pytest`. Prefer end-to-end tests over many small unit tests.
+
+## Approach
+
+1. Create a small but real dataset in a temporary directory (`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`,
+   removed in `tearDown`/`tearDownClass`). Reuse the dataset-creation helpers of the nearest
+   existing test file instead of writing new ones.
+2. Load it through the public API: `get_train_dataset`, `get_val_dataset`, `get_loader`,
+   `get_savable_loader`, ... Use `WorkerConfig(rank=0, world_size=1, num_workers=0)` for simple
+   cases.
+3. Assert on the samples that come out (keys, content, order or determinism), not on internals.
+4. Where the change can affect it, also cover:
+   - save/restore of the loader state (`save_state_rank` / `restore_state_rank`): the samples
+     after restoring must equal the samples the uninterrupted loader produces.
+   - multiple workers (`num_workers > 0`) and multiple ranks (`world_size > 1`).
+5. A bug fix needs a test that fails without the fix.
+
+## Rules
+
+- Only cover behavior that matters to the user. Not every small piece of functionality needs its
+  own test.
+- Do not add a micro-test per function or test private helpers in isolation.
+- Extend an existing test file before creating a new one. New files go in `tests/` as
+  `test_<topic>.py` and need the NVIDIA license header (see an existing test).
+- Keep datasets tiny and tests fast; no network, GPU or external data.
+- Reference pattern: `tests/test_dataset.py`.
+
+## Running
+
+```bash
+just test                                                    # full suite
+uv run python -m unittest tests.test_dataset                 # one module
+uv run python -m unittest tests.test_dataset.TestDataset.test_loader_close  # one test
+```
+
+Run `just fix` and `just check` after editing tests. When reporting verification, include the exact
+command and its result.

+# Repository Guidelines
+
+Instructions for AI coding agents working in this repository. Humans should read
+[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); everything there applies to agents as well.
+
+## What this project is
+
+Megatron Energon is a general-purpose PyTorch data loader for large-scale, multi-modal training.
+It was built for [Megatron-LM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM), but it is a standalone
+library and must stay usable with any PyTorch training loop. Do not introduce dependencies on
+Megatron-Core.
+
+Its core promises are: loading large datasets efficiently, blending many datasets, distributing
+work across nodes, ranks and workers, and exact reproducibility and resumability (save/restore of
+the loader state). Any change must preserve these.
+
+Layout of `src/megatron/energon/`:
+
+- `flavors/`: dataset formats (webdataset, jsonl, crude datasets) and sample types.
+- `recipe/`: recipe (YAML) parsing and dataset blending configuration.
+- `task_encoder/`: user hook for decoding, cooking, encoding and batching samples.
+- `wrappers/`: composable iterable datasets (batch, blend, shuffle, packing, ...).
+- `loader.py`, `savable_loader.py`, `worker.py`: data loaders, worker setup and state saving.
+- `cache/`, `epathlib/`, `av/`, `media/`, `decoders/`: file caching, local/remote paths,
+  audio/video decoding, media metadata, sample decoding.
+- `cli/`, `tools/`: the `energon` command line tool.
+
+User documentation lives in `docs/source` (Sphinx, MyST markdown).
+
+## Environment and commands
+
+- The project is managed with `uv` (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`). Never hand-edit `uv.lock`.
+  Use `uv run ...` instead of activating `.venv`.
+- The `justfile` is the canonical entry point:
+  - `just dev-sync`: sync all extras into `.venv`.
+  - `just fix`: apply ruff fixes, formatting and license headers. Run it after every change.
+  - `just check`: ruff lint and format check. Must pass.
+  - `just test`: full test suite.
+  - `just check-commits`: check sign-off and commit message format of your branch.
+- Tests use `unittest`, not `pytest`. Run focused tests with dotted names:
+
+  ```bash
+  uv run python -m unittest tests.test_dataset.TestDataset.test_loader_close
+  ```
+
+- When reporting verification, include the exact command that was run and its result.
+
+## Code
+
+- Clean, maintainable, readable code is the bar. Follow the conventions of the surrounding
+  module; match its naming, structure and comment density.
+- Keep diffs minimal and on-topic: no drive-by refactors, reformatting or renames outside the
+  task, no commented-out code.
+- Every new `.py`, `.sh` and `.md` file needs the NVIDIA license header, and user-facing changes
+  need documentation in `docs/source` (skill: `writing-docs`).
+- Prefer end-to-end tests through the public API over micro unit tests (skill: `writing-tests`).
+
+## Commits and pull requests
+
+- Always commit with `git commit -s` using Conventional Commits (skill: `committing`). Never add
+  `Co-Authored-By` (or similar) trailers for AI assistants.
+- Never push, open pull requests or issues, or comment on GitHub unless the human explicitly asks
+  you to (skill: `opening-a-pr`). Leave the human review checkbox unticked.
+
+## Skills
+
+Task-specific guidance lives in `.agents/skills/`: `writing-tests`, `committing`, `opening-a-pr`,
+`writing-docs`. `.claude/skills` is a symlink to it for Claude Code.
